For smart adjustable gimbal recessed lights that work with Alexa or Google Home, I'd prioritize three things: how far the light can tilt, the quality of the light (brightness and color), and whether it connects directly to your smart home or requires a hub.

One important distinction: many recessed smart lights can change brightness and color but cannot physically aim the beam. Since you're looking for gimbal lights, I'd focus on models that offer both physical tilt adjustment and smart control.

Best options I'd consider
Best overall

40° tilt · 810 lumens · RGB + tunable white · CRI 90

$129.99 / 4-pack

My top choice for kitchen lighting, general illumination and directional accent lighting. Its 45° beam is more focused than a typical downlight.

$139.99 / 4-pack

Best for artwork, sloped ceilings and wall washing. The narrow beam gives it a spotlight effect, but it's less suited to broad room illumination.

90° tilt · 270° rotation · 780 lumens · dual-light design

$139.99 / 4-pack

Best for ambient effects. Combines a tunable-white main light with a separately controllable multicolor auxiliary light.

View at Best Buy

20° tilt · 355° rotation · RGBWW

$159.99 / 4-pack

Best if you need a 6-inch fixture instead of 4-inch. The tradeoff is less tilt adjustment.

View at Best Buy

All four models are advertised as compatible with Alexa and Google Assistant. The gimbals are manually aimed; smart control handles brightness, color, scenes and scheduling, not motorized aiming.

What I'd check before buying

Ceiling cutout: 4-inch and 6-inch are nominal sizes; check the actual cutout and installation depth.

Existing housing: Determine whether you need a canless fixture with junction box or a retrofit for an existing recessed can.

Wall dimmers: These Wi-Fi models generally need constant power and aren't designed for traditional dimmer switches.

Smart-home reliability: Most of these use 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Zigbee, Thread or Matter. For a large installation, that distinction matters.

One caveat: Lumary dominates the currently identifiable smart-gimbal options, but I wouldn't automatically consider it the most reliable lighting brand for a whole-home installation without comparing longer-term support and warranty coverage.

For smart adjustable gimbal recessed lights that work with Amazon Alexa or Google Home, I'd focus on lights that offer three things:

Physical tilt and rotation so you can aim the beam at walls, artwork, or specific areas.

Smart control for dimming, color temperature, or RGB colors through Alexa or Google Home.

Reliable connectivity, preferably Wi-Fi, Matter, or Zigbee rather than an obscure proprietary app.

One important distinction: most smart gimbal lights let you adjust the direction manually, while brightness and color are controlled by voice or app. Motorized aiming is much less common.

What I'd check before buying

Existing ceiling opening: 4-inch and 6-inch refer to fixture classes; check the manufacturer's actual cutout dimensions.

Wall switches: Many of these smart fixtures cannot be used with traditional dimmer switches. Dimming happens through the app or voice assistant.

Light quality: Look for CRI 90+ if these will illuminate kitchens, countertops, or artwork.

Reliability: Integrated LEDs can be expensive to replace if a driver or LED module fails. Check warranty coverage before buying a large quantity.

Connectivity: Alexa/Google compatibility does not automatically mean Matter support or full local control.
